title: Truth or Trash: 'Juiced' with OJ Simpson, Bigfoot Bounty, man tied to cellphone tower

FILE - O.J. Simpson leaves court after closing arguments for his trial at the Clark County Regional Justice Center on October 2, 2008 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Steve Marcus-Pool/Getty Images)

In this segment on ARC Rochester, Christian Garzone presents us with news stories — all but one of which are true — and asks us to guess the false one.

You got ‘Juiced!'

Who here remembers prank shows like Candid Camera and “Punked”? Basically hidden cameras tape people in the midst of a practical joke – and there’s a celebrity who comes out letting the person know they’ve been duped. Back in 2004, there was a show filmed like this called “Juiced” with none other than OJ Simpson. OJ would do things like put on white face and prank people, then reveal himself to folks as OJ. It didn’t go over well! The show never made it to air.

Chinese stove has weird way to remind you it’s been left on

At the Chang-Sha expo, a company debuted a new mini stove for tight quarters that can sense weight. When pots have been taken off and the stove is left on for more than 5 minute, it emits a pleasant citrus odor and beeps. However, something went amiss and at the expo—a sulfur odor was smelled. The stench, startling people at the expo who thought a gas leak was in progress. The company is not sure what was behind the bad smell — it was not a gas leak — and the company is now fixing that issue.

Man wanted — after getting intimate with rubber duck in stranger’s hot tub

Georgia police are looking for a man who they say was infatuated with a rubber duck in someone’s hot tub. The man is wanted for trespassing on the property, taking a dip, and stealing luxury towels. Police say according to video he became “obsessed” with a rubber duck in the process... “intensely interacting” with the toy.

Hard Mountain Dew is giving away $1 million dollars if you can prove Bigfoot exists

I texted this to our friend Charles “Snake” Stuart this morning as a heads-up. Hard Mountain Dew is offering a $1 million prize to anyone who can provide verified proof that Bigfoot exists. The brand is launched its first-ever “Bigfoot Bounty” on September 15, giving Bigfoot hunters across the US until November 30 to submit evidence of the legendary creature. A blurry photo will NOT be enough they say. There must be things like footprints, DNA, clear video, etc.

Villagers arrested for tying technician to cell phone tower

In a protest over bad cell phone connections going on for two years, villagers in India tied a technician to a pole. They laid a trap for him to pull this off. The technician was ultimately freed by the police, with six locals being taken into custody over the incident.
